question.prompt: In the set \(\{1,2,2\}\), the element 2 is written twice. According to the distinctness property, can it count as 2 different elements?

solutions.explanation: The elements of a set are distinct. \(\{1,2,2\}\) and \(\{1,2\}\) are the same set, and the repeated 2 counts as only 1 element.
solutions.title: Distinctness of set elements
